note: Planning-only manifest. Every scenario is planned; NONE has been executed and spec 112 is still not_started. All 26 scenarios originate verbatim in spec.md section 7 and are mirrored into scopes.md under the scope that delivers them; this manifest is the contract entry, not evidence. linkedTests and evidenceRefs are empty in every entry and that is the literal truth: no test file exists for this feature, so naming one would be a claim rather than a plan — the same reason every scopes.md Test Plan row reads 'none yet'. requiredTestType and testPlanRow name the first-pass Test Matrix row that must prove the scenario at implementation time; testCommand is this repo's canonical command for that category, recorded here because scopes.md deliberately removed its Command column (a path-shaped token in a matrix row makes the traceability guard report every scenario as mapped to a real test file, which would be a false green). The separate Regression E2E table in scopes.md is NOT duplicated here; it is additional coverage keyed by the same ids and remains traceable in that file. changeType is set by one mechanical rule so it is checkable rather than a judgement: 'fix' iff at least one scopes.md row naming that scenario also names a section-3 E-observation the scenario must fail against, otherwise 'new'. behaviorTraits and obligations are deliberately NOT declared — see F-112-TRACE-04.
openFindings: F-112-TRACE-01 — Scenario ids SCN-112-A01 … SCN-112-E06 do not match the shipped scenario-manifest schema id pattern ^SCN-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$, because spec.md section 7 groups them by letter. All 26 violate it. The ids are analyst-owned and established across spec.md, scopes.md and design.md; they are NOT renumbered here. Sibling 111 records the identical divergence as F-111-TRACE-02.

F-112-TRACE-02 — schemaVersion is 3, matching siblings 108, 109 and 111, while .github/bubbles/schemas/scenario-manifest.schema.json declares schemaVersion const 1 and requires per-entry keys id/title/requiredTestType. Every sibling ships scenarioId instead of id, and the Gate G057 counter in guards/control-plane-checks.sh counts "scenarioId" occurrences, so conforming to the schema's key name would make this manifest invisible to the gate that reads it. Consistency with the siblings and with the gate was chosen over conformance to a schema that nothing in this repo applies. The divergence is recorded, not silently resolved; reconciling schema and shipped shape is a framework-owned decision.

F-112-TRACE-03 — The schema is not enforced against downstream spec manifests in this repository. yaml-schema-validate.sh resolves REPO_ROOT to .github/bubbles and globs specs/**/scenario-manifest.json beneath it, so it reports 'SKIP specs/**/scenario-manifest.json (none present)' while 108, 109, 111 and now 112 sit under the real specs/ tree. That is why the F-112-TRACE-01 and F-112-TRACE-02 divergences are latent rather than blocking. The affected script is framework-managed and is not modified here.

F-112-TRACE-04 — behaviorTraits and obligations are deliberately NOT declared. Deriving a proof-obligation matrix requires design decisions this packet still lists as BLOCKING and open (F-112-UNIT-01, F-112-UNIVERSE-01, F-112-108-01, F-112-FLAG-01): until the unit of a capability and the independently derived universe are settled, a declared trait set would be invented rather than derived. scenario-obligation-lint.sh is inert when no traits are declared, so nothing is weakened by the deferral; declaring traits the design has not settled would be the fabrication it exists to catch.

F-112-TRACE-05 — SCN-112-A02 is claimed by SCOPE-04, SCOPE-06 and SCOPE-07; SCN-112-A03 by SCOPE-04 and SCOPE-06; SCN-112-D03 by SCOPE-03 and SCOPE-07. Each is placed here under the scope whose Use Cases section defines it, with the other claimants recorded in alsoClaimedBy. scopes.md already reports these multi-claims and explicitly leaves them uncorrected; this manifest mirrors that decision rather than resolving it.

F-112-TRACE-06 — The changeType rule is applied literally, and two of its results are worth naming rather than hand-adjusting. SCN-112-C02 and SCN-112-C03 read as repairs of the live three-authority navigation divergence (E11-E14), but no scopes.md row binds either id to an E-observation, so the mechanical rule reports them as 'new'. SCN-112-E06 reads as new behaviour, but it shares a Regression E2E row with SCN-112-E05 that names E9, so the rule reports it as 'fix'. The rule was kept mechanical so the field stays checkable; the three mismatches are recorded here instead of being quietly overridden.

F-112-TRACE-07 — The 'Descriptor record' Test Matrix row must also prove R-112-03 (a stable identifier survives phrasing, navigation, alias and exposure churn) and R-112-07 (the registry carries identity and policy only, never user content, readiness facts or session scope). Neither obligation is stated by SCN-112-A01 or SCN-112-A06, so neither id carries it in tracesTo — borrowing an unrelated id would make the trace look complete while proving nothing. Whether section 7 gains scenarios for R-112-03 and R-112-07, or the row stands as a DoD-asserted obligation like the 'Alias uniqueness' row already does, is an analyst decision.
